Step 1: Calculate the total cost of the loans. Jim gets $50,000 in loans per year for 4 years.
Total loans = $50,000/year * 4 years = $200,000.

Step 2: Calculate the money lost from not working while in school (opportunity cost). Jim made $25,000 a year before college, and it took 4 years.
Money lost = $25,000/year * 4 years = $100,000.

Step 3: Calculate the total financial deficit by the time he finishes college (loans + lost wages).
Total deficit = $200,000 (loans) + $100,000 (lost wages) = $300,000.

Step 4: Calculate his new income after college. His college degree tripled his previous income of $25,000.
New income = $25,000 * 3 = $75,000 per year.

Step 5: Calculate his *increase* in earnings per year (the extra money he makes compared to his pre-college job) that goes toward paying off the deficit.
Previous income = $25,000 per year.
New income = $75,000 per year.
Additional yearly income = $75,000 - $25,000 = $50,000 per year.
*(Note: Alternatively, if he lives on the same $25,000 as before, the remaining $50,000 of his new salary can go directly toward paying off the $300,000 total).*

Step 6: Calculate how long it takes to earn the money equivalent to the total deficit using his additional yearly income.
Time = Total deficit / Additional yearly income
Time = $300,000 / $50,000 per year = 6 years.

Final answer: 6
